why: Same hashed context-mixing model as the record, scored by verify.py on 8 fresh seeds that were not used for any choice: dev mean 1.1261, 95% CI +-0.0003, SD 0.0004, a gain of about 0.018 on the record's 1.1445. Changes, with single-seed estimates from sequential tests on seed 11 (seed noise about 0.0005, so the smaller ones are rough): masking contexts that reach back before the window start, which zero padding made look like story starts (-0.005, eval-only on saved params); raw-hash in-window votes with five stages tuned on dev (-0.0025); batch 128 with table updates half as often (-0.002); mixer learning rate 1.2e-2 (-0.001); folding rare bytes into 76 softmax classes instead of 130, which buys more training bytes (-0.004); decaying the table learning rate over the run (-0.003). Caveats: about 40 variants were compared, almost all on one seed, and the five vote-stage constants were fitted on dev (half-split check showed a similar gain on the untouched half), so dev is slightly optimistic. The last change, spending spare parameter capacity on rows, was within noise. A per-window paired comparison with the record on one seed gives a gain of 0.0187 with SE 0.0008, but dev window sampling alone has SE 0.0057 on the level, so the sealed-split mean may sit roughly +-0.008 from this dev figure for reasons common to every entry; the gain over the record is the more reliable quantity.
